### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/cli`, touching **6** documentable anchor(s).

**20** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json d67b94280a2f2b2f1d4a3497142511ede21b8d42`.

⛔ **4** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `os validate (command, 53 pages)`
- **5** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **25** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json d67b94280a2f2b2f1d4a3497142511ede21b8d42` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `13e745e72a4aaeec5c8d459d391c6ca6b6badd7a` — the merge of head `69f413fb76e2dca9f395ba0116aef4d85d6182c8` into base `d67b94280a2f2b2f1d4a3497142511ede21b8d42`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 13e745e72a4aaeec5c8d459d391c6ca6b6badd7a && git checkout 13e745e72a4aaeec5c8d459d391c6ca6b6badd7a
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin d67b94280a2f2b2f1d4a3497142511ede21b8d42 69f413fb76e2dca9f395ba0116aef4d85d6182c8 && git checkout -B drift-repro d67b94280a2f2b2f1d4a3497142511ede21b8d42 && git merge --no-ff 69f413fb76e2dca9f395ba0116aef4d85d6182c8

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json d67b94280a2f2b2f1d4a3497142511ede21b8d42
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs d67b94280a2f2b2f1d4a3497142511ede21b8d42` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `69f413fb76e2dca9f395ba0116aef4d85d6182c8`
Local-runs: none

Inputs read: card #20825 (body; triage `5908852656`; retriage answer `5923151807`; the seat's claim `5923350718`; the landing note `5923331640`; os-dev-report `5924182672`); the predecessor PR #21003 (body, landed `b84b240b2a`) and its record `5922950314`; PR #21049 (body, the 6-file list, two commits `ec1d965497` and `69f413fb76`) and the net diff `git diff 2f2fa11d75..refs/review/pr-21049` (+411 / −58); the spec at `origin/main` (`packages/spec/src/data/picklist.zod.ts`, `stack.zod.ts`), the load path (`packages/core/src/artifact-packages.ts`, `packages/runtime/src/artifact-collections.ts`, `packages/metadata/src/plugin.ts`, `packages/cli/src/utils/view-container-names.ts`), the parity roster, both changeset gates, ADR-0087's launch-window section, and the head's check-runs. Source context was read by sha only (`git show`, `git grep` on `origin/main` and `refs/review/pr-21049`), never from the working tree.

### ① Derived judgments

**(a) The new walk over `picklistExtensions` in `packages/cli/src/utils/picklist-references.ts`.**
- *It follows the field walk's load path by construction, not by a parallel branch.* `bodiesOf` is untouched by this diff: it still branches on `parsed.packages !== undefined` (the resolver's own test, the one `view-container-names.ts` and `resolveArtifactPackageOrder` make) and yields the top-level body for a one-package stack or each `packages[i].manifest` body through `artifactPackages`. The new code sits inside `referencesOf`, which runs once per body, so the extension walk takes exactly the bodies the field walk takes and cannot take others. Hence: a one-package stack's top-level `picklistExtensions` are judged, each `packages[]` body's own are judged, and a top-level `picklistExtensions` beside `packages[]` is not (pinned negatively in the unit file).
- *Is that the loader's reading of a top-level collection beside `packages[]`?* It is the reading every author-time judge in this file family makes, and it is the one the field half shipped under record `5922950314`: `resolveArtifactPackageOrder` returns only the `packages[i].manifest` bodies when `packages` is present, and the metadata door registers each body under its own id. Measured bound, stated here rather than hidden: the metadata door also runs a residual sweep over the top level for registry-kind items no body claims (registered under the artifact's manifest id, with a logged warning that the artifact's two halves disagree), and the runtime's `resolveArtifactCollections` folds a top-level array together with the bodies'. Neither path reaches `picklistExtensions` today: the loader registers neither `picklists` nor `picklistExtensions` (PENDING #19519, the waiver in `scripts/check-stack-collection-maps.mjs`), and `PLURAL_TO_SINGULAR` records that extensions merge into their target rather than register as a type. In a `composeStacks(…, { manifest: 'preserve' })` artifact the top level is the additive flattening of the same bodies, so what the per-body walk judges is the same set of entries. The negative pin therefore encodes the precedent's reading, identical for a field and an extension, which is what the fold asked for. The residual-sweep edge (a top-level entry no body repeats) is a bound shared with the field walk and with `view-container-names.ts`, not new here; see ③.
- *Same declared set, same arm.* `declared` is still the union of every body's `picklists` (sibling packages included, the ADR-0130 co-ownership reading) and `known.has(ref.picklist)` is the one resolution test for both sites. The outside-dependency arm is `judged.outside`, computed per declaring body, so an unresolved `extend` is refused when that body names no dependency outside the artifact and is an `info` `picklist-reference-unverified` notice otherwise; a sibling's outside dependency does not soften it (pinned). The coarse trigger is untouched, as triage ruled (`5923151807`: a recorded line).
- *The schema, read.* `PicklistExtensionSchema` (`picklist.zod.ts:114`) is a `strictObject` of `extend: SnakeCaseIdentifierSchema` and `options: z.array(SelectOptionSchema).min(1)`, with the aliases `picklist` / `target` / `name` / `extends` folded into `extend` at the parse, so the parsed stack the judge reads carries `extend` and nothing else. `picklistExtensions: z.array(PicklistExtensionSchema).optional()` on `ObjectStackDefinitionSchema` (`stack.zod.ts:360`), compose disposition `concat` (`:1035`), and `MAP_SUPPORTED_FIELDS` deliberately excludes it (it keys by `extend`), so there is no record form and the `Array.isArray(extensions)` bound is exact. The `typeof extend !== 'string' || extend === ''` skip is unreachable post-parse and harmless.
- *The walk is where the outside-dependency arm belongs most.* An extension is how a package adds to a list it does not own, so the `info` arm is the honest verdict for an `extend` aimed at a dependency outside the artifact; the header says so.

**(b) The rule id is reused (`picklist-reference-unknown` / `picklist-reference-unverified`), not a sibling.** Right. What is judged is one fact (a name that resolves to no picklist the stack declares) with one cure class and the same two verdicts; a second id would split one class of verdict for every consumer keyed on `errors[].rule` and `warnings[].rule`, and nothing in the repository registers these ids in a ledger (`git grep` on `origin/main` finds them only in the judge, its pins and the pending changeset). The finding says which key carried it in all three places a consumer reads: `where` is `picklist extension "X"` against `field "obj.f"`, `path` ends in `picklistExtensions[N].extend` against `.fields.f.picklist` (prefixed `packages[I].manifest.` for a body), and the message opens with `extend: 'X'` against `picklist: 'X'`. A consumer that must count by key reads `path`, which is mechanical. The per-site sentences (`wordingOf`) differ only in the consequence and the hint, as they should: an extension gets "remove the entry" where a field gets "give the field inline `options`".

**(c) `validate.ts` / `compile.ts` touched.** Compelled: the heading literal `A field names a picklist this stack does not declare (N references)` stands over `printAuthoringRuleErrors` for every refusal in the set, so it would be false for an `extend` refusal and for a mixed set; `A picklist reference names a picklist this stack does not declare` is true for both. Grep on `origin/main`: the old literal appears on the two source lines only; no test, doc or changeset quotes it (`names a picklist` elsewhere is the liveness ledger's `authorHint` and a spec pin, both about fields, both untouched). The diff on the two commands is the literal plus the step 2d / 3a-bis comments; the call (`judgePicklistReferences(result.data)`), the notice capture, `printPicklistReferenceNotices`, the `--json` envelope and the exit are unchanged, and the `--strict` list is not touched. The parity roster scans bare identifiers either command calls: no new identifier is called (`judgePicklistReferences` is already a `SHARED_NON_REGISTRY_GATES` row, `printError` already `NOT_A_GATE` presentation), so no registration is owed and the dispatch's "only if the call or printing must change" allowance is met by the printing.

**(d) Pins and ablations.**
- Unit, 10 new (6 in the one-package describe, 4 in the `packages[]` describe): the resolving control, the refusal naming extension / list / declared lists / path, a stack declaring no picklist, a field and an extension in one pass, neither hiding the other, the outside-dependency notice, sibling-package resolution, the inside-only refusal, the declaring package's own dependencies, and the top-level-beside-`packages[]` negative pin. Asserted by rule id, severity, `where`, `path` and the names in the message, not by the sentence.
- Doors, 5 new over a real `os` process (11 now): a resolving `extend` validates and builds with the artifact carrying `['industry']`; a dangling `extend` is refused by `os validate --json` (exactly one error, `picklist-reference-unknown`, `where` naming `industy`, `path` `picklistExtensions[0].extend`), by the text face (exit 1, the extension and the path on stdout), and by `os build --json` (exit 1, same rule, and `dist/objectstack.json` absent). The fixture's manifest declares no `dependencies`, so the refusal arm, not the notice, is what the door pins exercise.
- Would they red without the walk? Yes, and the counts are consistent with the tests as written: disabling the extension walk leaves the controls and the negative pin green (they assert emptiness) and reds the seven unit pins and three door pins that assert a refusal or a notice, which is the dev's 7 / 12 and 3 / 8. Disabling the `packages[]` branch reds the two old and two new per-package pins that need a body and, by making the top-level branch judge the top-level entry, reds the negative pin too, which is the dev's 5 / 14 and proves that pin is not vacuous. Read off the test file, not run (Local-runs: none); the dev's ablations ran on committed fixes with restore proven.
- The before / after rows in the report (exit 0 and artifact written at `2f2fa11d75`; exit 1 and no artifact at the head, control unchanged) are the dev's measurement; the door file is the standing pin of the same facts.

**(e) The changeset `.changeset/20825-cli-picklist-extend.md`.** `@objectstack/cli: minor`; a `feat(cli)!:` title carrying `(#20825)` in the sibling form; `Clause-②: no (narrowing — …)`; the `adr-0087: not-required (no-migration-prescription)` marker with its reasoning in the comment; the BREAKING banner naming the convention; the FROM state (both commands passed, `os build` wrote the artifact), the TO state (exit 1, `picklist-reference-unknown`), and a one-line fix with the three cures the hint offers; the "which extensions are judged" paragraph (load path, sibling resolution); the outside-dependency paragraph (`info`, in `warnings` and on the console, never gating, not under `--strict`). Every sentence is delivered at the head and none overstates: no runtime merge is claimed (commit `69f413fb76` corrected exactly that wording in the header). The disposition is the honest arm: no authorable spelling or type moves, `packages/spec` is untouched, and which list the author meant is not in the metadata, so `objectstack migrate meta` has nothing to rewrite; the same arm passed the gate on the predecessor with the same shape of "one-line fix" text.
The pending `20825-cli-picklist-kind.md` is byte-identical at the head (correct: it is PR #21003's input to the release and describes what that PR shipped). Re-read for sentences made false by this diff: none. Its title and FROM / TO name a field's `picklist`, which is still exactly what it judged; its "Which references are judged" paragraph names the two collections the field walk reads and does not say "only"; its rule-id sentence remains true. The two changesets compile into two adjacent entries of the same release, and the new one's "the rule a field's dangling `picklist` already gets" reads correctly in that order.

### ② Semver level

Right. `@objectstack/cli` `minor` with the BREAKING banner: `os validate` and `os build` newly refuse an input they accepted, an accept-set narrowing on two published commands, which AGENTS.md's changeset rule grades BREAKING and the launch-window convention ships as `minor` (`scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs` refuses `major`; ADR-0087's ratified section: pre-GA a break ships `minor`, the banner and the disposition carry the breaking-ness, not the level). `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` is the well-formed pair from the closed set and is the true one for this diff: nothing is accepted that was refused before, the judge's five exports are the same five names, no spec key, export or config field moves, and the one narrowing is declared with its banner, its one-line fix and its ADR-0087 disposition. `@objectstack/lint` is correctly absent: `packages/lint/**` is untouched.

### ③ Boundary flags

1. **Every `deviations` entry.** (i) Rule id reused: the claim left the choice to the dev on condition it is stated in the PR; it is, with the reasoning, and ①(b) finds it right. (ii) `validate.ts` / `compile.ts` touched: the claim allowed it when the printing must change; the refusal heading is the printing, it would be false otherwise, and the two step comments ride the same hunk; nothing else in those files moved (①(c)). (iii) Commit trailers in the `Claude-Session` + `Co-authored-by: Claude` form AGENTS.md prescribes, and the PR footer in the session-URL form: a reporting matter with no bearing on the head. (iv) Fresh worktree from `2f2fa11d75` while `origin/main` moved to `d67b94280a`: confirmed below, no path overlap and a clean merge-tree. (v) No label writes beyond the assignee; the labeler's four (`documentation`, `size/m`, `tests`, `tooling`) are the platform's; a changeset exists, so `skip-changeset` does not apply.
2. **The out-of-scope polish note.** `quoteNames([])` yields "names no picklist this stack declares (this stack declares no picklist)", redundant wording from PR #21003 that now applies to both sites. True, cosmetic, not a contract defect and not an authoring trap; "carrier: none, noted" is the right disposition for a wording nit, and leaving PR #21003's sentence alone kept this diff to the fold.
3. **`Fixes #20825` closes the card correctly.** Triage `5923151807` closed the card's ledger: "#20825 closes on PR #21003, plus the fold below. Nothing else." PR #21003 landed (`b84b240b2a`, items 2 and 3, item 1's ingest half measured true at base); the generator and scaffold half, the Tier H skills line and the `collectMetadataStats` row are #21018 (`pm:blocked` on #19519); the coarse outside-dependency trigger stays a recorded line by the same answer; the "neither `options` nor `picklist`" refusal was never on this card. This PR is the fold, delivered on both doors with the control and the negative pin triage's answer and the claim named. The landing note `5923331640` says the fold's PR closes the card with `Fixes`, and the head's `The card this PR closes must claim this branch` check is green against claim `5923350718`'s branch. Nothing triage left on the card is undelivered.
4. **Bounds carried forward, not closed here, no carrier owed by this card.** (i) The top-level-beside-`packages[]` residual edge in ①(a): the field walk, the view-container judge and now the extension walk all take the resolver's reading; if #19519's reader ever registers a residual top-level extension under the artifact's id, the judge's reading and the loader's diverge on that edge for both keys alike. That is #19519's reader to decide, and the right act is one sentence in the judge's header when that reader lands. (ii) The predecessor record asked for a header sentence on the nested `plugins[]` bound (metadata typed `unknown[]`, walked by no judge); this follow-up did not add it. Not a defect, as that record said; still worth the sentence on the next edit of the header.
5. **Scope and surface.** Six files, all inside the claim's named surface (`picklist-references.ts`, its unit test, the door file, the two commands under the printing allowance, one changeset); `packages/spec/**`, `packages/lint/**`, the generator, the scaffold and `collectMetadataStats` are untouched. No governed path (`Governed Surface Queue Guard` green). Head repo = base repo. +411 / −58, under the 5,000 threshold. Draft, not armed.

All seven required contexts `success`: `Lint & Repo Gates` (03:46:08Z, which carries `check:adr-0087-registration` and so re-validated the `not-required (no-migration-prescription)` arm against the changeset's own body), `TypeScript Type Check` (03:44:05Z), `Test Core` (03:46:44Z; shards 1/6 to 6/6 all `success`, which carries the cli unit tier, the parity roster and the door file), `Dogfood Regression Gate` (03:37:45Z; 1/3 to 3/3 all `success`, so no in-repo example stack is refused by the new walk), `Build Core` (03:32:39Z), `Temporal Conformance (live PG + MySQL)` (03:37:34Z), `Governed Surface Queue Guard` (03:31:40Z).
